title: Six years (unprinted)
venue: the coast community-college paper, Newport · the laundromat digest
logline: Six years. Five a week for nobody. The Anniversary strip nobody printed. It has corn in it anyway.

panels.composition: Wood's bedroom. The table. A stack of strips, thick, unstapled — a summer's worth. A tray of corn on top of it, like a paperweight. WOOD drawing. BARNABY.
props: a thick stack of unprinted strips
a tray of corn on top

image.prompt: a young man drawing at a bedroom table beside a thick loose stack of comic strips weighed down by a paper tray of corn, a small dog under the table, brush-pen black and white

panels.composition: The stack. Dated in the margins. June, July, August. None stapled. None copied.

image.prompt: close-up of a thick stack of hand-drawn comic strips with dates in the margins, none stapled, edges uneven

balloons.text: Six years. Nobody's printing it. I'm still doing five a week. That's either discipline or a diagnosis.

image.prompt: a young man talking to a small dog while drawing at his table

panels.composition: The stack, the corn, the dog, the man at the long surface. #1's last panel for the sixth time. Nobody will see this one.

image.prompt: a wide quiet view of a young man at a long table with his back turned, a stack of strips and a tray of corn beside him, a dog underneath, black and white, no words
image.notes: Box 5. The divider before this strip in the book reads: Box 5 is full. None of it ran.
